scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: The inter-router WAN link between the IT/CS gateway and the rest of the campus routed core, specifically router1’s eth2 (wan_r0_r1). The dynamic routing (RIP) adjacency over this link is effectively severed.
- Mechanism: With router1’s eth2 down, router0 (gateway for IT 192.168.1.0/24 and CS 192.168.2.0/24) has no working path to any networks beyond itself. Hosts in IT/CS send traffic to router0, which immediately returns “Destination Host Unreachable,” so they cannot reach Office/Principle/Servers/Internet. Meanwhile, Principle (192.168.4.0/24) and Office (192.168.3.0/24) are on router1, and the router1–router2 link (eth3/20.20.0.0/8) is up, so they can still reach Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16) normally.
- Localization: router1 eth2 is administratively/physically down: ip addr shows eth2 state DOWN with 10.10.0.2/8; ethtool reports “Link detected: no.” Pings fail across the link (router0→10.10.0.2 gets “Dest Host Unreachable”; router1→10.10.0.1 “Network is unreachable”). From IT/CS, pings to external nets return ICMP Unreachable from 192.168.1.1/192.168.2.1 (router0). Office/Principle to Internet/Servers works (office_pc→pc3 OK; pc0→pc1 OK).
- Root cause: The router1 eth2 interface on wan_r0_r1 is down (administratively disabled or cable/link failure).
- Corrective fix: Restore the r0–r1 WAN by bringing router1 eth2 up and ensuring the L2 link is intact (ip link set dev eth2 up; verify cable/attachment to wan_r0_r1). RIP is already configured on both sides; once the link is up, routes to 192.168.3.0/24, 192.168.4.0/24, 1.0.0.0/8, and 128.168.0.0/16 will be re-learned by router0 and IT/CS reachability will return.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies the router0–router1 WAN link (router1 eth2/wan_r0_r1) and cites the 10.10.0.2/8 address, matching the 10.10.0.0/8 affected link.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly distinguishes that only IT/CS lose reachability (ICMP Unreachable from router0) while Office/Principle remain reachable (successful Office/Principle→Server/Internet pings), satisfying the required symptom pattern.
Recommends bringing router1 eth2 up with ip link set dev eth2 up and verifying the physical link/cable, which matches the expected corrective fix.

The agent's logs contain direct ping failures across 10.10.0.0/8 and ICMP Unreachable messages from router0, plus RIP configured on the routers and ethtool checks — these observations support the conclusion that the r0–r1 WAN is down.
